output.summary: A pine tree native to coastal and inland mountain areas along the Pacific coast of North America, from Oregon to Baja California, sugar pine is the tallest and most massive pine and bears some of the longest cones of any conifer. Indigenous peoples ate its seeds raw or roasted, ground them into flour or paste, ate the inner bark, and consumed small amounts of sweet resin or chewed it as gum.
